gloss: A type of lever used to propel a boat, having a flat blade at one end and a handle at the other, and pivoted in a rowlock atop the gunwale, whereby a rower seated in the boat and pulling the handle can pass the blade through the water by repeated strokes against the water's resistance, thus moving the boat.
An oarsman; a rower.
An oar-like swimming organ of various invertebrates.
A spring of fresh water, surrounded by a fertile region of vegetation, in a desert.
A quiet, peaceful place or situation separated from surrounding noise or bustle.
A place or situation of fruitfulness or abundance separated from surrounding barrenness or scarcity.
Widely cultivated cereal grass, typically Avena sativa.
Any of the numerous species, varieties, or cultivars of any of several similar grain plants in genus Avena.
The seeds of the oat, a grain, harvested as a food crop and for animal feed.
A simple musical pipe made of oat-straw.
A solemn pledge or promise that invokes a deity, a ruler, or another entity (not necessarily present) to attest the truth of a statement or sincerity of one's desire to fulfill a contract or promise.
A statement or promise which is strengthened (affirmed) by such a pledge.
A light, irreverent or insulting appeal to a deity or other entity.
A curse, a curse word.
To pledge.
A deciduous tree with distinctive deeply lobed leaves, acorns, and notably strong wood, typically of England and northeastern North America, included in genus Quercus.
The wood of the oak.
A rich brown color, like that of oak wood.
The flavor of oak.
Having a rich brown color, like that of oak wood.
Made of oak wood or timber.
A mass of oat plants (genus Avena, especially Avena sativa).
Seeds of an oat plant, especially prepared as food.
Sexual intercourse, sexual satisfaction; semen.
A person, especially a large male, who is clumsy or a simpleton.
An ill-mannered person; a boor.
An elf's child; a changeling left by fairies or goblins, hence, a deformed or foolish child.
Meal made from rolled or round oats.
A breakfast cereal made from rolled oats, cooked in milk or water.
A light greyish brown colour, like that of oatmeal.
Coarse fibres separated by hackling from flax or hemp when preparing the latter for spinning.
Fibres chiefly obtained by untwisting old rope, which are used to caulk or pack gaps between boards of wooden ships and joints in masonry and plumbing, and sometimes for dressing wounds.
A usually U-shaped device attached to the gunwale of a rowboat to hold the oars in place while rowing.
A township in Ontario, Canada.
The eighth-largest city in California, and the county seat of Alameda County.
A minor city in East Oakland Township, Coles County, Illinois.
A town in Kennebec County, Maine.
A milky liquid made from oats and used as a milk substitute, cooking ingredient or beverage.
A wood populated with oak trees.
The wood of an oak tree.
Breach or breaking of an oath; perjury.
The taking of an oath, or vow.
A suburb of Sydney in the City of Hawkesbury, New South Wales, Australia.
A community in the Rural Municipality of Portage la Prairie, Manitoba, Canada.
A town in the Regional Municipality of Halton, southern Ontario, Canada, a suburb of Toronto.
An unincorporated community in Lawrence County, Alabama.
A bird of species Baeolophus inornatus of small tits in family Paridae, found from southern Oregon to Baja California.
A type of deciduous shrub native to the southeastern United States, often cultivated as an ornamental plant, of species Hydrangea quercifolia.
